Team — sketched a concrete option for discussion. Key points: 
1) Baseline commit: 6 months at current effective tokens/month average, then quarterly step-ups of 10% (staircase) for the remainder of the term up to a 30% total uplift cap.
2) Graceband: a 25% temporary overage buffer for any single month without triggering immediate re-tiering; graceband burnable up to two months per rolling 6-month window. Overuse triggers a rightsize review but not automatic punitive uplift.
3) Pricing: per-token price tiers decline with commit volume. Staircase increases count toward tier thresholds as they step, but graceband consumption is billed at a slightly higher temporary rate (midpoint between committed and overage).
4) Credits & good-faith: include a one-time reconciliation credit up to 5% of monthly usage if actual usage deviates >20% from forecast in the first two quarters.

I attached a matrix with sample numbers tied to Acuta's recent usage. If this looks good, we can formalize in the SOW language: "soft-commit staircase," "graceband protection," and an explicit reconciliation cadence.

-Karthik

Subject: Soft-commit staircase & graceband proposal

Sam — following our call today (thanks for the time), here’s the proposal we agreed to in principle. I’ve summarized next steps below and attached the draft SOW language and pricing sheet.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Term: 12 months starting 2027-01-01.
- Baseline commit: equivalent to your 3-month trailing average multiplied to monthly, recognized as committed tokens.
- Staircase: front-loaded variant — Month 1: +15%, Month 2: +8%, Month 3–6: +4% monthly until cumulative uplift reaches 30% cap.
- Graceband: up to 25% of committed tokens available per month billed at a temporary rate (10% above the committed per-token rate). Graceband consumption allowed up to two months in any rolling 6-month window.
- Redwood exposure cap: Redwood will cap fiscal exposure to 40% of a committed monthly spend in any single month; any sustained usage above that will trigger conversion discussion.
- Reconciliation: Monthly reporting; any variance >20% in first two quarters triggers a one-time invoice credit (applied to next invoice) up to 5% of the affected month.
- Visibility & controls: Console alerts at 60/80% graceband consumption, ability to programmatically disable graceband via API or opt-out in Console.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (MOP), redwood_pricing_matrix_q4.xlsx (finalized numbers), Acuta_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW baseline).

Next steps:
1) Monica to share clean SOW language & final matrix by 12/17.
2) Acuta to confirm acceptance of staircase shape and graceband rules by 12/22 so we can get legal & finance to finalize DocuSign by 12/29.
3) If accepted, kickoff checklist / migration plan to be scheduled for first week of Jan.

Sam — please reply to confirm you have what you need or flag any outstanding items. If procurement needs a hard worst-case number for modeling, we can produce a scenario table showing cost at 0%/25%/40% graceband usage.

Thanks — look forward to locking this in.

Best,
